problem: If $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are polynomials of degree $14$ and $8$, respectively,  the degree of $P\cdot Q$ is{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: If $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are polynomials of degree $11$ and $9$, respectively,  the degree of $P\cdot Q$ is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $P$ is a polynomial of degree $11,$ the leading term contains an ${x}^{11}.$

Since $Q$ is a polynomial of degree $9,$ the leading term contains an ${x}^{9}.$

In $P\cdot Q,$ the ${x}^{11}$ term in $P$ multiplies with the ${x}^{9}$ term in $Q$ to form a term containing ${x}^{11}\cdot {x}^{9}={x}^{11+9}={x}^{20}.$

Therefore, the degree of $P\cdot Q$ must be $20.$
